name: Emergency AC Repair
h1: Emergency AC Repair, Answered Day and Night
problem: the temperature inside the house is climbing and so is the risk of a heat illness
symptoms: Air is running but the house will not cool down
The outdoor unit is silent and the thermostat reads warm
The system shut off mid-afternoon and will not restart
Water or ice is around the outdoor unit after a storm
A burning smell when the system kicks on
firstStep: Set the thermostat to fan-only and open doors between rooms to move air. If the outdoor unit has stopped and you have a breaker panel, check the AC breaker once. Do not open the electrical compartment on the unit itself, and if you smell gas, leave the house and call the gas utility first.

name: AC Not Cooling
h1: AC Not Cooling: What Is Actually Wrong

alsoTargets.k: air conditioner runs but does not cool

problem: the system is running, so it looks like it is working, and the house is still hot
symptoms: Air blows from the vents but it is warm or room temperature
The thermostat is set to 72 and the house stays in the 80s
The outdoor unit runs continuously and never cycles off
Only some rooms are cool
The evaporator coil is frozen over and the fan has stopped
firstStep: Do not keep lowering the thermostat. If the indoor coil is frozen, dropping the setting makes the freeze worse. Turn the system off at the thermostat and let the coil thaw for a few hours, then try one cycle before you call. If it happens again within a day, the cause is mechanical and needs a technician on site.

name: AC Repair
h1: Same-Day AC Repair in Houston, Diagnosed Before It Is Repaired
title: Same-Day AC Repair Houston | AC Repair Houston
problem: something in the system has failed and guessing at it costs money twice
symptoms: The system runs but does not cool the house
The outdoor unit will not start at all
The blower runs but the compressor does not
Water pooling under or around the outdoor unit
The system cycles on and off in short bursts
firstStep: Write down what the system does, not what you think is wrong. Whether the fan runs, whether the outdoor unit starts, and whether the breaker holds are the three facts that narrow the fault down before anyone opens a panel. That list shortens the diagnosis.

name: AC Installation
h1: AC Installation, Sized for a Houston Home
problem: there is no working system, or the current one cannot be saved
symptoms: A home with no central air at all
An open addition, garage conversion or new build with no cooling
A replacement where the old unit is beyond economical repair
Rooms that stayed warm after a remodel or an addition
firstStep: Get a load calculation, not a tonnage number off a sales sheet. A Houston home with west-facing glass, a vaulted ceiling or a second story in the loop needs a different capacity than the same square footage in Sugar Land. A unit that is too large cycles short and never dehumidifies.

name: AC Replacement
h1: AC Replacement When Repair Is Not the Answer
problem: the system is old enough that repair money buys a few more hot months
symptoms: The outdoor unit is past its service life
The refrigerant is a discontinued type and parts are hard to source
Repairs on the same unit keep recurring
The unit runs on a circuit that is already at its limit
The indoor coil and air handler are the same age as the condenser
firstStep: Find the refrigerant type listed on the outdoor unit nameplate before you shop. Older Houston systems run R-22, which is no longer produced for new systems and is priced accordingly. Knowing this in advance prevents the quote from changing once the old unit is pulled.

name: AC Maintenance
problem: the unit works fine right up until the week it does not
symptoms: The unit has not been serviced in two or more years
The system was barely used through a mild winter
The outdoor coil is dirty and the system runs long
Ductwork or filters were changed recently and performance changed with it
You want the unit checked before the hottest stretch of summer
firstStep: Change the filter first, and then see how the system behaves. A clogged filter is the most common reason a system that was fine becomes a same-day call. If the symptom does not change with a clean filter, the maintenance visit is worth booking.

name: Condenser Repair
h1: Condenser Repair for the Outdoor Unit
problem: the part outside is the one doing the hard work, and it is the one in the weather
symptoms: The outdoor unit is humming but the compressor is not starting
The fan spins and blows but the unit never cools
The unit is running and there is a puddle of water under it
The cabinet is rusted through in coastal areas
The unit is loud when it starts and then shuts off
firstStep: Clear the debris off the coil and make sure the unit has clear airflow and is level. Do not hose the coil with a high-pressure wand, it bends the fins and makes the coil worse. Beyond that, condenser work is a technician job because it involves refrigerant and live electrical.

name: Compressor Repair
problem: the pump at the center of the system has failed and everything downstream depends on it
symptoms: The outdoor unit runs but no cooling reaches the house
The compressor is silent and the fan still spins
The unit trips its breaker right after starting
The compressor has been running continuously for days
There is a hum from the unit with no compressor sound
firstStep: Before replacing a compressor, find out why it failed. A failed compressor on a system with a dirty coil or a blocked condenser will take the new one with it. Ask specifically what the tech did to find the root cause, not just what part went in.

name: Refrigerant Leak Repair
problem: the system is losing the gas that makes it cold, and topping it up is not a repair
symptoms: The system needs refrigerant every few months
The outdoor unit runs constantly but the house will not cool
There is an oily residue or a dark stain near a line or coil
The unit was low on gas a month after a service visit
You hear a hissing sound near the outdoor unit or the lines
firstStep: Ask for the leak to be located, not just for the system to be charged. Recovering refrigerant, finding the leak and repairing it are three separate jobs, and a recharge without a leak repair means the same call again in a few months.

name: Refrigerant Recharge
problem: the charge is low and the system needs to be brought back to spec
symptoms: The system is short on refrigerant and was told it needs a charge
A recently installed unit that is not cooling as expected
The blower runs and the compressor starts but the air is warm
The system was serviced elsewhere and behaviour changed afterward
firstStep: A proper recharge means measuring the charge, not eyeballing it, and checking superheat and subcooling to confirm the system is actually holding the right amount. That measurement is also what tells you whether the system is operating correctly or hiding a bigger fault.

name: Evaporator Coil Repair
problem: the coil inside the air handler is the part that actually makes the cold air
symptoms: Water dripping from the ceiling or the air handler
A frozen coil and a fan that has stopped
Musty or sour air from every vent
A visible green or grey slime on the coil
Water pooling in the air handler pan
firstStep: A frozen coil is usually a airflow or refrigerant problem, not a coil problem. Cleaning a frozen coil and calling it fixed is the most common way this gets handled badly. Ask what is causing the freeze to come back.

name: Blower Motor Repair
problem: the motor that moves the air has failed and the house has no air at all
symptoms: The thermostat says the system is on but nothing blows
A grinding, squealing or rattling noise from the air handler
The blower runs at one speed only and not at the other
The system works on the fan setting but not on cooling
The blower has started making a rasping sound
firstStep: A blower motor that is pulling too much current can take the capacitor and the motor together. If the motor is hot to the touch after a short run, stop using it. Ask whether the replacement includes the capacitor and the relay, which are the two cheap parts that usually go at the same time.

name: HVAC Electrical Repair
problem: the fault is electrical, and electrical faults do not care what the refrigerant level is
symptoms: The breaker trips when the system starts
The outdoor unit does not start and there is no sound
A humming outdoor unit that never kicks in
A scorch mark on a capacitor or contactor
The system works at one temperature setting and not another
firstStep: Do not keep resetting the breaker. If it trips again, leave it off. A tripped breaker on an AC unit is a short somewhere in the outdoor unit, and that needs a technician with the right meter and the training to work on live capacitors safely.

name: Condensate Drain Repair
problem: the water the system pulls out of the air has nowhere to go
symptoms: Water dripping inside the house from the air handler
A puddle under the outdoor unit that is not rain
Water staining the ceiling below a vent
A musty smell that gets worse when the system runs
The unit shuts down and a warning light comes on
firstStep: If the drain is backed up, the pan float switch may have already shut the system down. Do not try to clear a drain line with a shop vac or a garden hose. Note where the water is coming from, since an attic unit and a unit in a closet fail differently and the water often travels before it shows.

name: Thermostat Installation
problem: a good system on a bad thermostat never performs the way it should
symptoms: The system runs constantly and the house is still warm
The schedule on the thermostat is ignored
The thermostat needs replacing after a remodel
A smart thermostat that will not connect to the system
The thermostat is old and the wiring does not match
firstStep: Photograph the existing wires before anything is removed, and note which ones go to which terminal. Most thermostat problems in Houston homes are a mismatched wire set left from a previous install, and that photograph is what makes the swap quick.

name: Ductless Mini-Split Installation
problem: there is no ductwork to run and the rooms that need cooling have none
symptoms: A room addition, garage or shop with no cooling
An older Houston home with no central air and no attic space for ducts
A second floor that is a different temperature from the first
A home where ductwork would mean opening finished walls
Multi-unit cooling planned room by room
firstStep: Find out whether there is a place for the outdoor unit that is out of direct sun and drains away from the house. In Houston, the condenser placement matters as much as the sizing, because a unit in the afternoon sun works far harder than one in shade.

name: Ductless Mini-Split Repair
problem: a head-mounted system is the only cooling in the room and it has stopped
symptoms: The indoor head blows but does not cool
Water drips from the head onto the wall or floor
The outdoor unit is running but the head stays in fan only
A loud rattle or a whistling noise from the head
The head shows an error code
firstStep: Clean the filter and make sure the head is not obstructed. Mini-split heads in a Houston bedroom collect dust and pet hair quickly, and a blocked filter freezes the coil inside the head. If it is still not cooling after that, the error code on the head tells the technician where to start.

name: Heat Pump Repair
problem: one system handles both heating and cooling, so a fault takes out both
symptoms: The heat side runs but the cooling side does not
The system runs constantly in both directions
Ice on the outdoor unit in the warm months
The backup heat strip runs all the time
The system will not switch from heating to cooling
firstStep: Note whether the problem follows the mode. If cooling fails and heating still works, that points to the reversing valve and the refrigerant side. If both fail together, it usually points to a control or electrical fault. That distinction saves a lot of diagnostic time.

name: Commercial AC Repair
h1: Commercial AC Repair and Rooftop Units
problem: a building system serves a lot of people at once and the clock is the constraint
symptoms: A rooftop unit that has shut down and will not restart
Tenant complaints that only some offices are hot
A chiller or cooling tower that is not keeping up
A building with no preventive maintenance schedule
Ice forming on a packaged rooftop unit
firstStep: Get the maintenance history before you call. On a commercial unit, the difference between a failed part and a failed system is usually a year of deferred filter changes. A contractor who reads the service log first is working from facts rather than symptoms.

name: AC Cleaning
h1: AC Coil Cleaning and Condenser Service in Houston
title: AC Coil Cleaning Houston | AC Repair Houston
problem: a dirty coil is the cheapest performance loss in the whole system
symptoms: The outdoor coil is packed with leaves, lint or dust
The system runs long and never reaches setpoint
The indoor coil has visible grime on the fins
Water is dripping from the unit after it shuts down
The unit has not been cleaned since it was installed
firstStep: Look at the outdoor coil. If the fins are visibly packed with debris, a garden hose on a gentle setting and a soft brush will clear a surprising amount before anyone opens anything. Keep the unit clear of a shrub or a fence too, because a blocked condenser works far harder for the same result.
